title: Two-beat to four-beat playing, Dave Jones and the riverboat
summary: Ridgley says they played two beats to the bar until Dave Jones, back from up north, persuaded them to use four. He mentions working with Jones on a steamboat and returning from St. Louis for Celestin at Suburban Gardens.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: When you played was it all four, four instead of two beats, two measure, always four beats?
Most of our time was like that time, two beats.
Two beats, two measure. Yeah, yeah. You wouldn't, would you beat your foot as you played? Yeah. Would you only beat two beats, two measure rather than four?
No, yeah. At the beginning we started but after that we added, we said after David got with us, we just added that first time. Four beats, two measure. Four beats.
Dave, the saxophone player, Dave Jones.
Did he talk you into doing that or why did you?
Yeah, he did, he had been up to Lyon a long time, you know. And when he come back, of course, him and I was together on the Strait for the Boat together, you see. We worked together on the boat.

Yeah. Steamboat. I went up to St. Louis. But Solstern was at Suburban Garden, you see. And he sent for me to come back here, you see. And I made my money by coming back to the Suburban Garden, you see. We did on the boat, the Boat didn't pay much. We was glad to have him. But we made good at the Suburban Garden.
And after that time did you always play four beats rather than two?
After Dave Jones you said? Four, yeah. Four. Which did you like better? Did you like the four better?
Four, four at a time, you see. Oh yeah, it was better. It was the best. The whole piece went faster too. Yeah, and the people liked it, just put more in it.
I see. You could get more notes. It made you all play more notes.
